Before I played this game I read a review that described it like maintaining a garden; now having beaten it, that is indeed an apt description. Once you get your playthrough off the ground it is largely self-perpetuating, and any maintenance you give it helps it grow optimally and more productively. But that's just any proper idle game; with NGU Idle, the garden it gives you to grow is pretty janky- adapting to its weird balance and incredibly slow yield can be tough- but it is a really, uniquely, human crafted experience, and there will probably never be another idle game that successfully imitates the vibe of this one.
